stem:
Wahid's school bag costs $\mathrm{₹}600$. GST is charged at $12\%$ of the bag cost.

What must he decide before calculating the GST amount?

options.text: Only the multiplier $12/100$, without naming any whole in rupees.
That $12\%$ gives the same rupee amount on every bill, so the whole does not matter.
That the whole is $\mathrm{₹}600$, so the GST is $(12/100) \times 600$.
Start from a guessed GST amount and reverse to invent both the bag cost and the percent.

teacher.key_rationale: A percentage amount needs a named whole: here ₹600, so GST is (12/100)×600. Using only the multiplier, claiming the whole never matters, or reversing from a guessed amount miss that base choice.
